topic: Can satellite orbital configurations optimize ML-based QoS by reducing propagation delays for latency-sensitive traffic classes?
consensus_response: Satellite orbital configurations can optimize ML-based Quality of Service (QoS) by reducing propagation delays for latency-sensitive traffic classes. This is achieved through the consideration of physical mechanisms influencing satellite orbital configurations, such as array factor and interference in satellite communication systems. By analyzing the budget implications of design choices, we can reduce propagation delays and improve QoS for latency-sensitive traffic classes. A path selection mechanism aware of satellite link characteristics is necessary to mitigate high fixed latencies on links, which negatively impact QoS. This approach can be combined with modulation scheme adaptation using deep learning to further optimize ML-based QoS.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the challenges in providing Quality of Service (QoS) in converged satellite and terrestrial networks due to high fixed latency of satellite links, neglecting link characteristics such as latency or jitter. Current QoS architectures focus solely on managing available capacity, ignoring path selection based on satellite link characteristics.
